lineage: Encryptor shares an identical codebase/builder with Morpheus (SentinelOne); ransom-note template resembles Underground Team
summary: HellCat is a small, high-profile double-extortion crew (personas Rey, Pryx, Grep and others) active since late 2024. Its signature access path is logging into corporate Atlassian Jira with credentials that infostealers (Lumma, RedLine, Raccoon, StealC) took from employees or third parties; this hit Schneider Electric, Telefonica, Orange, Ascom and Jaguar Land Rover. Exploits against exposed applications (Jira, PAN-OS CVE-2024-0012/9474) and phishing are also reported. On hosts, a multi-stage PowerShell chain with an AMSI bypass reflectively loads a Sliver stager; data goes out over SFTP or to cloud drops before the Morpheus-shared encryptor runs.
uniqueTraits: Access to Atlassian Jira with infostealer-harvested (sometimes years-old, third-party) credentials
Staged PowerShell chain s1.ps1 > Payload.ps1 > Isma.ps1 (AMSI bypass) > Shellcode.ps1 that reflectively loads the Sliver shellcode 'Stager.woff'
HKCU Run value named 'maintenance' for persistence
Exfiltration over SFTP and to the actor-run site waifu[.]cat; bulk theft often without encryption
Encryptor identical to Morpheus: no extension change, _README_.txt in C:\Users\Public, self-deleting '_-_.bat'

chain.techniqueName: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
chain.procedure: Upstream stage: infostealers (Lumma, RedLine, Raccoon, StealC) on employee or third-party machines harvest browser-saved Jira credentials that HellCat later reuses.

atomics.note: Browser credential theft across Chrome/Firefox/Edge, matching infostealer behaviour (local ART T1555.003 #16)

atomics.testName: Simulating access to Chrome Login Data
atomics.note: Access to Chrome Login Data (local ART T1555.003 #4)

chain.procedure: Logs in to the victim's Atlassian Jira with the stolen credentials, sometimes a supplier's account (e.g. JLR via LG Electronics staff credentials dating back years).
chain.noAtomicReason: Logging in to SaaS/on-prem Jira with stolen credentials has no ART equivalent; validate with Jira audit-log analytics (new geography/device, dormant accounts) and credential-exposure monitoring.

chain.procedure: Exploits exposed systems such as Atlassian Jira; a related actor discussed PAN-OS CVE-2024-0012 / CVE-2024-9474 against US victims.
chain.noAtomicReason: No local Atomic test exploits these CVEs; validate with vulnerability scanning / patch-state checks or a purple-team exploit range, not ART.

atomics.note: Downloads a macro-enabled phishing attachment (local ART T1566.001 #1)

chain.procedure: Multi-stage PowerShell chain from an open directory (s1.ps1 disguised as an executable > Payload.ps1 > Isma.ps1 > Shellcode.ps1), each stage downloading and running the next.

atomics.note: PowerShell download cradles, as used to chain the stages (local ART T1059.001 #9)
Fileless PowerShell script execution (local ART T1059.001 #10)

chain.techniqueName: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
chain.procedure: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run value 'maintenance' points to the malicious script.

atomics.note: Adds a Run key value (local ART T1547.001 #1)

chain.techniqueName: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
chain.procedure: Isma.ps1 bypasses the Antimalware Scan Interface before shellcode is loaded.

atomics.note: AMSI bypass via amsiInitFailed (local ART T1685 #16)
AMSI bypass by patching AmsiScanBuffer (local ART T1685 #78)

chain.procedure: Shellcode.ps1 downloads Stager.woff (Sliver shellcode) and runs it in memory without touching disk.

atomics.note: Reflective PE injection from PowerShell (PowerSploit) (local ART T1620 #2)

chain.procedure: Sliver C2 implant establishes the command-and-control channel (Bridewell tracks thousands of linked Sliver connections).
chain.noAtomicReason: The local catalogue has no Sliver implant atomic; generic user-agent tests do not reproduce Sliver traffic. Validate with network detections for Sliver C2 profiles in a C2 lab.

chain.procedure: Netcat used for communication and lateral movement between hosts.
Creates new SSH users with admin rights and unique SSH keys on Linux systems, with backdoor malware as a fallback.
chain.noAtomicReason: Local catalogue is Windows-focused and has no SSH authorized-keys/account atomic; validate on Linux with auditd rules for useradd and authorized_keys writes.

chain.techniqueName: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
chain.procedure: Stages and compresses bulk data before theft (about 40 GB of compressed data reported in the Schneider Electric case).

atomics.testName: Compress Data and lock with password for Exfiltration with 7zip
atomics.note: Password-protected 7-Zip archive of staged data (local ART T1560.001 #4)

atomics.testName: Compress Data and lock with password for Exfiltration with winrar
atomics.note: Password-protected WinRAR archive of staged data (local ART T1560.001 #2)

chain.procedure: Exfiltrates over SFTP (described by Pryx as common) and to the actor-run site waifu[.]cat or other cloud/TOR drops.

atomics.note: Pushes a file out with the built-in sftp.exe client (local ART T1105 #36)

chain.procedure: Custom 64-bit encryptor (code identical to Morpheus) takes a path argument, uses Windows CNG/BCrypt, does not change file extensions and drops _README_.txt in C:\Users\Public.

atomics.note: Drops a ransom note; exercises note-creation detections without encrypting (local ART T1486 #5)

chain.procedure: Self-deleting batch file '_-_.bat' removes the payload after encryption.

atomics.testName: Delete a single file - Windows cmd
atomics.note: Deletes a file from cmd (local ART T1070.004 #4)
